setlist.title: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **New Speedway Boogie** (2 reviews): Reviewer says the band revived it just before this run, and the crowd nearly fainted; The drop from Truckin' into New Speedway Boogie is described as powerful and special [6][15]
- **Foolish Heart** (1 review): Reviewer says Phil takes over and makes Foolish Heart special [15]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): The jam coming out of Truckin' explodes, more than most jams from that song [11]
- **Drums** (1 review): Reviewer rates the drums and space segment among the best in a while, with Phil's solid bass lines [12]

## The recordings

- **gd91-05-10.sbd.ladner.6257.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 182 min; rated 4.33/5 by 30 [1]. Said about its sound: By the end of Jack Straw the board mix becomes solid and lush; vocals are solid; Sound quality is superb with nice mixing [9][12]
- **gd1991-05-10.149676.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 185 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1991-05-10.166598.mtx.seamons.ht167.flac1644**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 184 min [4]. Said about its sound: SBD mix fluctuates at set openings, improving in set 1 from They Love Each Other; a loud drum boom was reduced in Jack Straw; EQ applied to audience boominess and SBD high end; SBD levels shifted in Sugar Magnolia and Baby Blue; 1:10 segment repeated at Space to Wheel [4]
- **gd1991-05-10.149670.sbd.pearson-healy.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 21 songs; 185 min [3]

## Around the show

- Crowd reacted wildly to New Speedway Boogie, which the band had brought back just before this run [6]
- Reviewer credits Bruce (Hornsby) with bringing out Jerry's playing at this show [7]
- Cites Robert Greenfield's book Dark Star: the band took off from late April Las Vegas shows through spring and summer 1991 [17]
- New Speedway Boogie was a hoped-for rumor in the parking lots since the February Oakland shows [17]
- Calls it a favorite nineties tape; says Hornsby and Garcia show strong chemistry, with the second set from Foolish Heart to Drums standing out [6]
- Describes it as the opening night of a three-night stand, followed by 5/11 and 5/12, with similarly good sound [7]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd91-05-10.sbd.ladner.6257.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > DAT > CDR > WAV > SHNv3 [1]
- **gd1991-05-10.149676.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  April 24, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [2]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; several sets of masters combined to make the show complete [2]
- **gd1991-05-10.166598.mtx.seamons.ht167.flac1644**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Soundtrack Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Soundtrack > Final Cut for pre- and post-mix EQ > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT… [4]. Also: Soundboard and audience matrix; Charlie Miller's SBD transfer patches a Cold Rain and Snow dropout, dated 4/24/20 [4]
- **gd1991-05-10.149670.sbd.pearson-healy.miller.flac2496**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  April 24, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [3]
